title: Data Visualization Team Project
section: Distribution of U.S. Natural Gas Storage
text:
Distribution of U.S. Natural Gas Storage
Research Question: How are weekly U.S. natural gas storage levels distributed from 2010–2026?

Why We Chose This Question
We wanted to examine the distribution of U.S. natural gas storage levels over time. By looking at the weekly data, we can identify which storage levels occurred most frequently throughout the 2010–2026 period.


How We Created the Graph
We used Microsoft Excel to organize the weekly natural gas storage data and create a histogram. The histogram groups storage levels into ranges, allowing us to see how frequently different storage levels occurred.


What the Graph Shows
The histogram shows the frequency of different U.S. natural gas storage levels from 2010–2026. It helps identify which storage ranges occurred most often and how the weekly storage levels were distributed throughout the period.

section: Natural Gas Storage Levels Are Slightly Left-Skewed
text:
Natural Gas Storage Levels Are Slightly Left-Skewed

Research Question: How are weekly U.S. natural gas storage levels distributed from 2010–2026?

Why We Chose This Question
We wanted to examine the distribution of U.S. natural gas storage levels over time. Looking at weekly data allows us to identify common storage levels and understand how the data is distributed.


How We Created the Graph
We used Microsoft Excel to organize the weekly natural gas storage data and create a histogram. The histogram groups storage levels into ranges, allowing us to see how frequently different storage levels occurred.


What the Graph Shows
The histogram shows that natural gas storage levels are slightly left-skewed, with most observations concentrated around 3,000 Bcf. This means that storage levels near 3,000 Bcf occurred more frequently than some of the lower storage levels.
